Bots

How to write a bot for Concord: run the headless concord --bot and drive it with newline-delimited JSON from any language.

A bot in Concord is a peer. It has its own identity, it is invited into a guild the way a person is, and it reads what that membership lets it read: the guilds it was invited to, nothing more. Its messages are end-to-end encrypted like anyone's, and the guild can kick it like anyone. Nothing about encryption changes to make room for it, because nothing has to.

concord --bot is the front end for a script. It boots an identity and the network, then speaks newline-delimited JSON: one event per line on stdout, one command per line on stdin. Logs go to stderr. Any language that can read and write lines can drive it.

#Create one

Build the headless binary (make cli puts it in bin/concord), then give the bot a data directory and passphrase of its own:

export CONCORD_HOME=~/bots/dice        # the bot's identity and history live here
export CONCORD_PASSPHRASE='…'          # unlocks it; required, since a bot has no terminal to type it in
concord --status                       # creates the identity, prints its fingerprint

CONCORD_BOOTSTRAP and CONCORD_DISABLE_MDNS work as they do for concord --serve. One data directory is one bot; never run two processes on the same one.

#Invite it

Copy an invite code from the guild in the app, exactly as you would for a person, and hand it to the running bot:

{"cmd":"join","invite":"CI1ARDg…"}

A member who can admit it must be online at that moment, as for anyone. The membership is stored in CONCORD_HOME, so later runs need no invite. Both examples below take the code as an optional first argument and send this for you. Keep the bot running for a little while after it first joins: like a person's client, it needs a moment to settle into the guild.

#Events (stdout)

Every line is one JSON object with a type.

typeWhenFields
readyOnce, at startfingerprint, peerId, name, guilds (see list)
messageSomeone else postedguildId, guild, channelId, channel, messageId, sender (fingerprint), senderName, content, sent (RFC 3339, UTC), replyTo?, kind?, dm?
editA message the bot saw was editedguildId, channelId, channel, messageId, sender, content
deleteA message the bot saw was deletedguildId, channelId, channel, messageId
memberSomeone joined or left a guild the bot is inaction (join/leave), guildId, guild, fingerprint, name
guildThe bot joined or left a guildaction, guildId, guild
repliesAnswer to a commandsee below; carries the command's id
errorA command failed or a line was malformederror, id (if the line had one)

Notes:

  • The bot never receives its own messages, from this process or any other device of its account.
  • kind is absent for ordinary chat. system is a notice such as "has joined the guild"; filter on kind if you only want what people typed.
  • History is not reported: neither what arrives by sync nor anything sent more than a few minutes before the bot started. A bot does not answer week-old commands on restart.
  • sender is the authenticated identity. senderName is self-chosen and decorative; never authorize anything by it.

#Commands (stdin)

One JSON object per line, with cmd. Every command may carry an id (any JSON value); its reply and any error echo it back. Unknown fields are an error, so typos are not silently ignored. A malformed line produces an error and the bot carries on. Lines over 1 MiB are discarded.

cmdFieldsReply
sendchannel, text, replyTo? (a messageId){"type":"sent","channelId","messageId"}
reactchannel, message (a messageId), emoji{"type":"ok","cmd":"react"}. Toggles: reacting twice removes it.
joininvite{"type":"joined","guild":{…}}
list—{"type":"guilds","guilds":[{"id","name","dm"?,"channels":[{"id","name","type"?,"ref"}]}]}
membersguild (id or name){"type":"members","guildId","members":[{"fingerprint","name"}]}
nametext{"type":"ok","cmd":"name"}. Sets the bot's display name.
quit—{"type":"ok","cmd":"quit"}, then the bot exits.

A channel is any of:

  • a channel id, such as the channelId of a message you are answering;
  • "Guild/#channel" (guild by name or id; the # is optional), as in the ref that list returns;
  • "#channel", when exactly one of the bot's guilds has a channel of that name.

Names match exactly, then ignoring case. A name that matches more than one channel is an error, not a guess.

The bot exits cleanly on quit, at the end of stdin, and on SIGINT or SIGTERM.

#Example: ping, in shell

POSIX sh and jq. Answers !ping with pong, as a reply.

#!/bin/sh
# pingbot.sh [invite-code]: answer "!ping" with "pong", as a reply.
set -eu
fifo=$(mktemp -u) && mkfifo "$fifo" && trap 'rm -f "$fifo"' EXIT
concord --bot <"$fifo" | {
  if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then jq -nc --arg c "$1" '{cmd: "join", invite: $c}'; fi
  jq --unbuffered -c '
    if .type == "message" and .content == "!ping" then
      {cmd: "send", channel: .channelId, text: "pong", replyTo: .messageId}
    elif .type == "error" then ("error: " + .error + "\n" | stderr | empty)
    else empty end'
} >"$fifo"

#Example: dice, in Python

Answers !roll 2d6 with the roll, as a reply.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""dicebot.py [invite-code]: answer "!roll 2d6" with a roll, as a reply."""
import json, random, re, subprocess, sys

bot = subprocess.Popen(["concord", "--bot"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, bufsize=1)

def send(**cmd):
    print(json.dumps(cmd), file=bot.stdin, flush=True)

for line in bot.stdout:
    ev = json.loads(line)
    if ev["type"] == "ready":
        send(cmd="name", text="dicebot")
        if len(sys.argv) > 1:
            send(cmd="join", invite=sys.argv[1])
    elif ev["type"] == "error":
        print("error:", ev["error"], file=sys.stderr)
    elif ev["type"] == "message" and not ev.get("kind"):
        m = re.fullmatch(r"!roll ([1-9]\d?)d([2-9]|\d{2,3})", ev["content"].strip())
        if m:
            rolls = [random.randint(1, int(m[2])) for _ in range(int(m[1]))]
            send(cmd="send", channel=ev["channelId"], replyTo=ev["messageId"],
                 text=f"{ev['senderName']} rolled {sum(rolls)} {rolls}")

#Posting alerts

A bot that only posts needs no script at all. This turns every line appended to a log into a message, for as long as it runs:

tail -F alerts.log |
  jq -Rc --unbuffered '{cmd: "send", channel: "Ops/#alerts", text: .}' |
  concord --bot

Keep it running rather than starting one per alert. A bot that starts, posts and exits has had no time to find the guild's members, and the message waits in mailboxes instead of arriving.
